concerns.text: Task T006b introduces a 'random strategy' for dataset sampling if memory limits are exceeded. The spec's 'Assumptions' section mandates filtering for documents ≥ 32,000 tokens to test the ultra-long-context hypothesis. Random sampling of the filtered set (or unfiltered set) without explicit spec authorization constitutes a silent relaxation of the research scope, potentially violating the 'Distillation Fidelity' principle if the sample is not representative of the long-context distribution.

Task T028 mandates a fallback to the 'narrativeqa' dataset if 'hotpotqa' is unavailable. The spec (FR-007, SC-004) explicitly requires evaluation on a 'downstream long-context QA task (e.g., HotpotQA subset)'. Introducing 'narrativeqa' as a fallback without explicit spec authorization creates a scope drift; narrativeqa may not satisfy the 'long-context' constraint required by the research question, weakening the validity of the comparison against the dynamic baseline.

Task T031 describes a sensitivity analysis sweep that 'rebuilds index (using artifact data/processed/static_index.json)'. This phrasing implies overwriting the single static index artifact for each K value. The spec (FR-008) and Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) require that derivations produce new files and that raw data/derivations are preserved. Overwriting the artifact violates the 'Data Hygiene' principle and risks losing the specific index generated for a particular K value needed for reproducibility.

Task T013b is defined solely as a 'verify' function (`verify_edge_case_logging`) to assert log messages. The spec's 'Edge Cases' section requires the system to 'skip these or pad them to the minimum length, logging the action'. The task description fails to include the implementation of the actual skip/pad logic, only the verification of the log. This is a semantic weakening of the requirement; the task must implement the behavior, not just verify the log of a behavior that doesn't exist in the task scope.
